newsitem.title: UK: Tesco insists it will label gene foods.
newsitem.headline: Tesco insists it will label gene foods.

text.p: Tesco, Britain's leading food retailer, will label genetically modified foods, it said in a statement Thursday.
This policy will mean that suppliers will have to segregate ingredients like soya and maize into modified and unmodified groups, the company said.
"We shall continue to seek this from our suppliers and to lobby trade bodies on the issue," Tesco said.

Because segregation has been difficult to achieve in the short term, Tesco has introduced leaflets explaining the issues about genetically modified soya and maize and is making a list of products free of soya and a list of products containing no genetically modified ingredients available to its customers.
The chain has acquired stocks of unmodified soya to supply its bakeries and all its breakfast cereals are made from unmodified maize, it said.
On December 13, it announced that it was banning unprocessed genetically modified maize from animal feed within its producer group.

Tesco insists that it is not opposed to genetic modification. "Generally we support the introduction of genetically engineered foodstuff, where there are definite consumer benefits and when they have been judged safe by the relevant government organisations," Tesco said.
The move follows the introduction of a genetically modified form of soya by Monsanto Co in the U.S., and a genetically modified maize developed by Swiss chemicals group Ciba Geigy AG.
